task.description: Idiom/scope hard gate on ELIXIR-DEV's implementation of ISS-0444: two rescue clauses (claim_due_timer_ids/2, run_retention_sweep/1) added to lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, plus regression tests in scheduler_test.exs and scheduler/poller_test.exs.

result.summary:
Read the actual diff (not the paraphrase) and independently re-ran everything.

1) RESCUE SHAPE MATCHES DESIGN EXACTLY. `git diff main..HEAD -- lib/letflow/scheduler.ex` shows both `claim_due_timer_ids/2` and `run_retention_sweep/1` gain a `rescue error in Postgrex.Error ->` clause using `match?(%Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: code}} when code in [:undefined_table, :undefined_schema], error)`, an `else` branch `reraise error, __STACKTRACE__`, and (on match) `Logger.warning(message, schema: tenant_schema, reason: :schema_unavailable)` before returning `[]` / `{:error, {:schema_unavailable, tenant_schema}}` respectively. `require Logger` was added to the module head (confirmed absent before). This is byte-for-byte what §1/§3/§4 of the design specify.

2) IDIOM CONSISTENCY WITH pin_rebind.ex CONFIRMED BY DIRECT READ. Re-read `lib/letflow/engine/pin_rebind.ex:376-393` myself (not the design's paraphrase): `lock_projection_nowait/2` uses the identical `rescue error in Postgrex.Error -> if match?(%Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: :lock_not_available}}, error) do ... else reraise error, __STACKTRACE__ end end` shape. The scheduler.ex clauses are structurally identical (same rescue pattern, same match?/2-then-reraise control flow), differing only in (a) matching a list of two codes instead of one literal atom, and (b) adding a Logger.warning/2 call the pin_rebind.ex precedent doesn't need (it has no logging obligation) -- this addition is itself justified against a *different*, equally real precedent (alerts.ex:585-593's message-plus-keyword-metadata shape, re-confirmed by direct read: `Logger.warning("alert hook auth_secret_ref resolution failed...", component: "alert_delivery", ref: ref)`), not invented. Also cross-checked poller.ex:174's own `with_admission/3` precedent (`Logger.warning("poller admission capacity exhausted, skipping schema/operation", schema: schema_name, op: op)`) -- the scheduler.ex log calls use the same message+keyword-list shape with the same `schema:` key. Idiomatic, not a crutch: this is a narrow, symmetric application of an already-established in-repo pattern, not a new abstraction.

3) SUPERVISION: unaffected. No new process, no spawn, no change to `Letflow.InstanceSupervisor` or `Poller`'s own supervision tree. The fix is a pure function-local rescue inside an existing context module (Scheduler is not, and was never, a :gen_statem/GenServer -- it is plain business logic called from Poller's timer). No isolation collapsed.

4) TYPE-SAFETY: no new class of invalid state introduced. `claim_due_timer_ids/2`'s @spec is genuinely unchanged ([Ecto.UUID.t()] in, same out) and `run_retention_sweep/1`'s pre-existing @spec already covered {:error, term()} -- confirmed by reading both @specs directly, not just trusting ELIXIR-DEV's claim. No type-safety gap worth filing under docs/issues/ -- collapsing 'schema unavailable' into the existing all-zero poll_result() shape (design §2) is a deliberate, well-argued choice, not a representable-state gap: there is no timer-level outcome to encode a struct/enum around, and the design explicitly rejected a process-dictionary side channel and a tagged-tuple return for good reasons (would break every existing map-shaped caller).

5) SCOPE: confirmed via `git diff main..HEAD --stat` -- exactly `lib/letflow/scheduler.ex` (+35/-0), `test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs` (+137), `test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs` (+64), the design doc, and handoffs/registry.json. No edit to `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` or `lib/letflow/event_store.ex` -- matches ELIXIR-DEV's claim that neither needed changes (poller.ex's moduledoc claim becomes true in fact once this lands; archive/1 is EventStore's general-purpose primitive with ~9 test call sites that want a raise to propagate, correctly left alone). No new abstraction, no config layer, no behaviour introduced ahead of need -- this is squarely sized to the defect, not scope creep in either direction (the retention-sweep half is legitimately in scope per the design's own 'no additional complexity' criterion: the {:error, term()} branch already existed in that function's @spec).

6) MUTATION-TESTING CLAIMS VERIFIED BY READING THE TESTS THEMSELVES (not re-run, since re-running requires temporarily damaging working code -- verified instead that the asserted tests are structurally capable of catching the regression ELIXIR-DEV describes): `test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs`'s three new ISS-0444 describe blocks call `claim_due_timer_ids/2`, `poll_and_fire/1`, and `run_retention_sweep/1` directly against `never_provisioned_schema_name()` (a syntactically-valid, physically-never-created schema string) and assert both the non-raising return value AND `log =~ "tenant schema unavailable"` -- removing the rescue clause necessarily makes `Repo.all(query, prefix: tenant_schema)` / `EventStore.archive(...)` raise `Postgrex.Error` uncaught, which ExUnit surfaces as a real test failure (not a silent assertion mismatch), so these are genuine, non-vacuous regression tests. Same holds for `poller_test.exs`'s two blast-radius tests (bad schema registered before/after a real due-timer schema) and the retention blast-radius test -- each asserts the real schema's own effect (timer fired / event archived) still happens, which is only true if `Enum.each`/the sweep loop survives the bad schema without aborting.

7) POLLER_TEST.EXS FIXTURE (`registered_but_unprovisioned_schema_name!/0`) IS LEGITIMATE. Builds a real `Tenant` + `Registration` row pair directly via `Repo.insert!` (not `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1`, which always physically provisions) -- this is the correct, minimal way to reproduce backfill.ex's own documented 'Registration row exists but its physical schema no longer exists' edge case without a real CREATE-then-DROP-SCHEMA round trip. Cleanup is proper: `on_exit(fn -> Repo.delete_all(Registration where tenant_id) ; Repo.delete_all(Tenant where id) end)` removes both rows unconditionally regardless of test outcome, and since no physical schema was ever created there is nothing else to leak (no orphaned Postgres schema, no dangling `tenant_schemas` cache row beyond the two deleted rows). The `Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto)` call at the top of the helper is a documented, deliberate workaround for the DataCase-vs-provisioned_tenant/1 sandbox-mode-switch ordering issue, not an unexplained hack.

8) INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (run by me, in the foreground, real output, not reused from ELIXIR-DEV's report):
   - `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`: clean -- 'Compiling 186 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings.
   - `mix format --check-formatted`: clean, no output (no unformatted files).
   - `mix test test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler_req188_test.exs test/letflow/event_store_test.exs`: Result: 71 passed, 0 failures. Matches ELIXIR-DEV's reported count exactly.

No anti-pattern from docs/anti-patterns.md triggered by this change (reviewed the file; it has no entries applicable to rescue-clause/logging idiom).

JUDGMENT ON SKIPPING A SEPARATE TEST-DESIGNER PASS: I agree with ELIXIR-DEV's routing note. This is a small, symmetric, two-site mechanical fix reusing an already-established in-repo rescue idiom, and the tests already written cover: (a) both direct-call non-raising paths with log assertions, (b) both blast-radius orderings for the timer-poll path, (c) the retention blast-radius path, (d) explicit non-regression of the pre-existing `claim_due_timer_ids/2` length/1 assertions (re-run, still passing, unmodified). I independently confirmed test coverage completeness by reading every new test above rather than only trusting the summary -- coverage matches every scenario the design's §6 test-approach section calls for, including both relative orderings called out specifically to avoid a false-pass depending on Enum.each's row ordering. No coverage gap found. Routing straight to TEST-RUNNER for the full-suite confirmation is appropriate; a dedicated TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR pass would be redundant process overhead for a fix this narrow.
result.routing: Route to TEST-RUNNER for full-suite confirmation (mix test, whole suite) before Step Final. REVIEWER's idiom/scope/supervision/type-safety gate is satisfied; no rework needed.

gate_history.notes: Rescue shape verified byte-for-byte against design; idiom cross-checked directly against pin_rebind.ex:376-393, alerts.ex:585-593, poller.ex:174; scope confirmed via git diff --stat (scheduler.ex + 2 test files + design doc + handoffs only); mutation-testing claims verified by reading the tests themselves; poller_test.exs fixture confirmed to have proper on_exit cleanup and no leak risk; mix compile/format/test independently re-run in foreground -- 71 passed, 0 failures.
